name: libxml++
reason: No numeric comparison found. It is a C++ wrapper over libxml2 (LGPL-2.1, 81 stars); the README is build and install notes, the repo has examples/, tests/ and docs/ with no benchmark directory, NEWS has no performance entries, and the libxmlplusplus.sourceforge.net page makes no performance claim. No third-party shootout including libxml++ was reachable; at best its speed is libxml2's, and libxml2 is recorded separately.

name: libxo
listed_description: Allows an application to generate plain text, XML, JSON and HTML output using a common set of function calls. The application decides at runtime what output style should be produced.
reason: No performance claim at all. README, doc/*.rst (faq, intro, howto, formatting, options, example) and the repo (347 stars, BSD-2-Clause) contain no benchmark or numbers; the project sells a single format-string API for four output styles, not speed. A search for xo_emit against printf or cJSON found no published numbers.

name: magic_get
listed_description: std::tuple like methods for user defined types without any macro or boilerplate code.
reason: No numeric comparison found. The repo is a mirror of Boost.PFR (boostorg/pfr, BSL-1.0, 216 stars, last commit 2023-10-11); README and doc/pfr.qbk only compare code size and usability (hand-written db customization vs PFR) and describe the implementation, with no benchmark directory (test/ has config, core, core_name; misc/ has generators). Searches for PFR compile-time or runtime benchmarks found only documentation. Other reflection libraries (for example enchantum, qlibs reflect) use PFR or magic_enum as the baseline they beat, so no win by PFR exists in reachable sources. boost.org and the Boost mailing list were blocked.
